cryptohome: Expose mount operations in a single function. In order to move cryptohome mount operations out of process, first we need to expose them as a single function in the helper. The reason for this is pretty straightforward: when executing out of process, the helper needs to be able to carry out all the mount operations in a single invocation. The easiest way to ensure that this will be possible is to perform all mount operations as a result of a single function invocation. Then we change the function invocation to a helper executable invocation and we're done. This continues the work in the previous CL by transferring enough state to the MountHelper class to allow regular user mounts to be completed with a single call to the helper. In order to make the helper API less overly verbose, this CL also introduces an Options struct for the helper. As opposed to ephemeral mounts, where the entire *Inner function could be moved to the helper, for regular mounts the *Inner function does quite a bit of key manipulation. Per the design these should stay in cryptohome and not be done in the helper, so for regular mounts the helper calls happen inside of the *Inner function instead of fully replacing it. This is not a big deal since seam between the Mount class and the helper is still pretty obvious since key operations happen first and mount operations happen later. The next CL in the series will move unmount calls to the helper, in preparation for running things out of process (this is the plan at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hSUSuIQLZvH1OVwn7N8lDIT7lFUEeHkmFDXQduBccho/edit#.) This CL is a net addition of fewer than 100 lines. Most of it is code moved around. BUG=chromium:985492 TEST=Unit tests pass. TEST=Add new user to Chromebook successfully. TEST=Log in, create local data, log out. TEST=Log back in, local data is still present. UPSTREAM: Bluetooth: btrtl: HCI reset on close for Realtek BT chip Realtek RTL8822BE BT chip on ASUS X420FA cannot be turned on correctly after on-off several times. Bluetooth daemon sets BT mode failed when this issue happens. Scanning must be active while turning off for this bug to be hit. bluetoothd[1576]: Failed to set mode: Failed (0x03) If BT is turned off, then turned on again, it works correctly again. According to the vendor driver, the HCI_QUIRK_RESET_ON_CLOSE flag is set during probing. So, this patch makes Realtek's BT reset on close to fix this issue. factory_install: Also look for model name as cros_payload entry If <model>.json in cros_payloads/ exists, use it as the cros_payload metadata. Otherwise fall back to use <board>.json. This opens a way to create an RMA shim that has different payloads for different models that belongs to the same board, without changing the RMA shim structure and image_tool. We can create RMA shims and set the model model name in `--board` argument, and merge them into a multi-board shim. A problem for this approach is that all kernels have the same signing key and bootable on the devices, so only the first kernel will be used, but it will not be a problem if all models are using identical factory shims. vm_tools: sommelier: Support for active window requests. We add support for applications to request window activation. One legitimate us of this request is to foreground a window if the user e.g. opens a file in a pre-existing window. There are two common ways for windows to request this, either directly (via NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW) or indirectly (setting the urgency flag in their NET_WM_HINTS property). The former will only work if we advertise that "active window" is supported by this WM. Currently the request does nothing (except log a message). We will handle it in a future CL. tpm_manager: correct timing of destruction of |default_trunks_factory_| With async signal handling being enabled, for TPM2.0 default_trunks_factory_ doesn't get destructed in the same thread where it's initialized. As a consequence a DCHECK assertion in ObjectProxy failed. This fix addressed the issue the way as we dealt with the same issue in |AttestationService|. Specifically: 1. change |default_trunks_factory_| to a unique_ptr so we can control its life cycle strictly after the worker thread running and before its termination. 2. implement CleanUp in a base::Thread subclass where we call TpmManagerService::Shutdown.
